purpose: Remove a claim from active truth without deleting or rewriting historical evidence.

authorization.false: authenticated operator correction or evidence-verified contradiction required
authorization.superseded: verified replacement revision and lineage edge required
authorization.duplicate: content-equivalence proof and canonical replacement required
authorization.expired: deterministic temporal rule with bound source required
authorization.corrupt: hash or schema failure receipt required
authorization.policy: versioned deterministic policy and evidence receipt required

effects.history: Target payload and all earlier revisions remain immutable and queryable as non-active evidence.
effects.active_truth: Target, descendants, and claims in a targeted entry or revision are excluded.
effects.retrieval: History-only retrieval must label the statement as tombstoned and include reason/effective_at.
effects.derivatives: Transitive dependants become stale or superseded before any further use.
effects.index: Active indexes omit the target; historical indexes retain it with tombstone metadata.

closure_algorithm: Seed closure with the direct target.
For entry targets, add every revision and claim in the entry.
For revision targets, add every claim in the revision and descendant revisions.
For claim targets, add every claim whose derived_from_claim_ids reaches the target.
Add every derived artifact whose claim or revision dependencies intersect the closure.
Repeat until no new object is added.
invariants: A tombstone never deletes or mutates its target.
target_sha256 must match the target payload at creation.
Each tombstone has at least one evidence reference.
An unresolved or unauthorized tombstone fails closed and has no authority.
A target cannot have two different effective tombstones without an explicit conflict receipt.
Privacy tombstones suppress normal retrieval but preserve encrypted audit evidence.

resurrection.rule: A tombstone is never revoked in place. New evidence creates a new claim or revision with a new ID, explicit relation to the tombstoned target, and fresh authorization.
resurrection.active_truth_requirement: The replacement independently passes the complete active-truth gate.

rollback.rule: Rollback restores the pre-transaction snapshot and its tombstone set exactly; it never selectively removes a committed tombstone.
